title: Best Dating App Privacy Tools Compared
metaDescription: NordVPN, Signal and Burner compared for dating-app privacy: hiding your IP address, keeping your number private, encryption, device support and ease of use.
intro: Dating apps collect massive amounts of personal data, from your location to intimate preferences. Whether you're protecting yourself from stalkers, maintaining discretion, or simply valuing privacy, the three tools compared here each cover part of the problem.

products.name: NordVPN
products.tagline: VPN that hides your IP address and encrypts your connection
products.pricing: From about $3-$3.50/month (Basic, 2-year plan); renews at a higher price
pros: Hides your IP address from the apps and sites you use
Encrypts your connection, including on public Wi-Fi
cons: Paid subscription; introductory prices renew higher
Doesn't change your phone's GPS location, which most dating apps use
Like any VPN, adds some slowdown

products.name: Burner App
products.tagline: Second phone numbers you can give to matches and discard
pros: Easy to burn number and start fresh
cons: No free plan beyond a trial
Calls and texts aren't end-to-end encrypted

products.name: Signal
products.tagline: End-to-end encrypted messaging with disappearing messages
pros: Phone number hidden from others by default; usernames available
Disappearing messages for any chat, with an optional default timer
cons: Requires a phone number to register; a username can hide it from others
Requires both parties to use Signal
Only helps once you move a conversation off the dating app

verdict.summary: NordVPN scores highest on these five criteria, but the three tools protect different things. NordVPN hides your IP address and encrypts your connection, which matters most on public Wi-Fi; it doesn't change the GPS location most dating apps use to place you, so it won't hide where you are. Signal is second: when you move a chat off the dating app, you can share a username instead of your phone number, and messages are end-to-end encrypted, though your match has to install it too. Burner gives you a second phone number for calls and texts, so matches never see your real one, but its calls and texts aren't end-to-end encrypted.

pro_tips: Use NordVPN's Threat Protection feature to block known malicious and phishing sites, including links sent by fake profiles.
Create separate Burner numbers for different dating apps to compartmentalize your dating life and track which app led to unwanted contact.
Run reverse image searches on a match's photos in a private window while signed out, so the searches aren't tied to your accounts or saved in your browser history.
Set your VPN to a nearby city rather than across the world - extreme location differences can trigger dating app security flags.
Regularly burn and replace temporary numbers every few months, even if you haven't had issues - it's a proactive privacy measure.

faqs.question: Will using a VPN get me banned from dating apps?
faqs.answer: Most dating apps tolerate VPN use, but avoid extreme location jumps (like appearing in different countries daily) which can trigger security algorithms. Stick to nearby locations for best results. A VPN changes only your IP address: most dating apps place you using your phone's GPS, so a VPN won't move you on the map.

faqs.question: Can matches trace my real phone number through Burner?
faqs.answer: No, Burner creates completely separate phone numbers that aren't linked to your real number. However, some dating apps may detect virtual numbers during verification.

faqs.question: How do I safely research someone I matched with?
faqs.answer: Run a reverse image search, such as Google Lens or TinEye, on their photos to check they aren't copied from someone else, and look them up in a private window while signed out, so the searches aren't saved to your accounts or browser history. Some sites show people who viewed their profile while you're signed in; LinkedIn does unless you switch on private viewing.

faqs.question: Should I tell matches I'm using privacy tools?
faqs.answer: Use discretion based on your situation. For general privacy, explanation isn't necessary. For safety concerns (stalking, harassment), being upfront about boundaries is often better than deception.

faqs.question: What's the biggest privacy mistake on dating apps?
faqs.answer: Linking social media accounts and using precise location sharing. These create detailed profiles that can be used for stalking or identity theft even after you stop using the app.
